title: Exact coefficient adjunction and normalized sections at the integral point
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On the small pro-etale site $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $A_m=(R/\varpi^m)_s$ for $m\ge1$ and $B=\varprojlim_m A_m$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. For an $R$-module $M$ let $\underline M$ be its constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and put $L(M)=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M$, using sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; apply $L$ and $\Gamma=\Gamma(s,-)$ termwise to complexes.
Then $R$ is Noetherian (every ideal is finitely generated), $B$ is flat over $\underline R$ [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and $L$ and $\Gamma$ on $B$-module sheaves are exact. The constant-value maps identify $\Gamma A_m=R/\varpi^m$ compatibly with quotient transitions, and identify $\Gamma B=R$ by the ring map $r\mapsto(r\bmod\varpi^m)_m$. There is an adjunction $L\dashv\Gamma$ whose natural bijection sends $h:L(M)\to F$ to $x\mapsto h_s(1\otimes x)$ and whose inverse sends $t:M\to\Gamma F$ to $b\otimes x\mapsto b\,t(x)|_U$ on every site object $U$. These are the actual constant-extension maps: the unit is $x\mapsto1\otimes x$ and the counit is multiplication of restricted sections.

proof.text: Every covering sieve of the algebraically closed point contains the identity of the final object. Apply this to the equalizer and image sieves of the constant sheafification unit to prove bijectivity on final sections. Naturality of the sheafification unit gives the finite quotient-transition identity. The limit lift/projection identity gives the completed scalar formula. Joint injectivity of evaluated limit projections and the profinite-tower isomorphism give the completed scalar bijection.

proof.text: Reproduce the finite-constant continuous-function comparison in the coefficient universe max u (t+1): open fibres give local surjectivity, nonempty objects detect constants pointwise, and empty objects use the empty covering. The continuous-function presheaf is a sheaf by fpqc descent. Sheafification uniqueness makes this comparison natural for quotient ring maps. At each point an evaluated completed section gives a compatible residue family, hence an integer by the profinite-tower isomorphism. If a nonzero integer annihilates the section, the evaluated integer vanishes in the domain. Joint injectivity of the finite projections implies that the section vanishes. Thus each completed section module is torsion free over the PID, and hence flat. Locally lift the finitely many scalar coefficients of any relation to constants by intersecting their image covering sieves. The sectionwise flat module equational criterion factors this relation, and the constant unit sends its matrix to a local factorization over the constant ring sheaf. Apply the independent-universe local equational criterion.

proof.text: Construct the constant-module presheaf Hom equivalence by evaluation at the final object and restriction along its unique maps. Compose module sheafification with the proved sectionwise tensor/restriction adjunction to obtain the actual extension functor and normalized Hom formulas. Constant presheaves preserve finite limits objectwise, and module sheafification is exact. The existing independent-universe change-of-rings tensor comparison identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of extension with tensoring by the restricted coefficient unit. The flatness already proved in step 3 therefore gives exact extension; forgetting to abelian sheaves reflects finite limits. The adjunction gives finite colimits. Evaluating the two Hom formulas on identities identifies unit and counit. Independently use exact point sections and exact scalar restriction for exact Gamma. The additive exact functors preserve finite limits and colimits of unbounded complexes degreewise.

Clause 5 gives varpi^m R as the norm ball. Cauchy completeness gives R = lim R/varpi^m, and the zero ideal and zero tuple are covered. Step 2: lem-pur-proetale-finite-constant-sections gives sections C(|V|,A) for finite A, compatible with constants and restriction. Its transition maps match the pointwise residues by the sheafification universal property. Sectionwise inverse limits then give Gamma B = R by r -> (r mod varpi^m). Step 3: B(U) injects into Map(|U|,R), so it is torsion free and flat over the PID with no finite generation needed. Presheaves over the constant presheaf R are presheaves of R-modules, so the presheaf tensor is exact objectwise. lem-pc-sites-modules-sheafification-flat allows a presheaf ring, so B is flat over R_s. Rejecting the sectionwise-flat node, which needs a sheaf ring, is correct. Step 4: the constant-module-sheaf functor is exact for all modules on a small site. I checked balancedness, B(U)-linearity, the unique extension by the interface lemma over B, and both composites.
